title: Orthogonal decomposition by coordinate sets
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by a finite nonempty set, whose zero-indexed vector is constant one and whose vectors are orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For any nonnegative integer $n$ and any real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, the components of $f$ obtained by grouping its product-basis Fourier expansion according to the set of coordinates where the index is nonzero sum to $f$. The component indexed by each coordinate set $S$ depends only on the coordinates in $S$, and is orthogonal in the product probability inner product to every function depending only on a set $T$ properly contained in $S$.
